where: Exam traps, third bullet: "A prompt cannot supply facts the model never learned."
problem: This sentence contradicts Section 4 of the same chapter. RAG works exactly by pasting into the prompt facts the model never learned from its weights, and the model then answers from them. A student who reads both will be confused about what a prompt can and cannot do.
fix: Say: "Instructions alone cannot supply a fact. If a fact is in neither the weights nor the prompt text, no wording can produce it; instructions such as 'do not hallucinate' reduce confabulation but never remove it. Pasting the fact into the context (RAG) does work, because the fact is then in the prompt."

where: Section 4, after the two fixes (truncate, summarise)
problem: "Both lose detail; say so in the system message" is unclear: say what, and to whom? A student cannot tell what sentence to write in the system message.
fix: Say: "Both lose detail. Add a line to the system message telling the model that older turns may be missing, so it asks again instead of inventing an answer."
